decision: Do any of three 2025-2026 tabular foundation-model opponents (LimiX-2, TabImpute, TabPFN-3.5 long table with compound-structure embeddings) beat AnchorBoost on sparse three-point concentration-response completion? A win (k = 3, 194-chemical cohort, mean paired difference against AnchorBoost below zero) is reported as the headline and sent to the controller to be merged into the method; a loss is reported as measured.
status: Retrospective benchmark on public data. Each opponent's configuration is chosen on development fold 0 only and frozen in this file (amendments) before any fold 1-4 prediction is made.

task.kit: <local-input>/kit (README, score.py). 243 chemicals x 35 concentrations x 68 outputs; five fixed designs per chemical and k; curve MAE; read-only.
task.folds: Fold 0 (49 chemicals) for development; folds 1-4 (194 chemicals) for reporting; to predict fold f, train on every chemical with fold != f.
task.allowed_inputs: All cells of the training chemicals, the revealed cells of the one test design, and the test chemical's own structure (SMILES). No other test chemical enters a prediction.
task.scoring: kit score.py --versus all. Primary interval: identity groups (189 in the 194 cohort), 4,000 resamples, seed 0; chemical interval alongside. Comparators: AnchorBoost, interpolation, TabPFN-3.5 (S1), CNP, GP and Hill-EB on the 193 cohort.

shared_feeding.source: Feature blocks reuse S1's definitions (sota_baselines/tabpfn/tabpfn_run.py, read-only, copied with attribution into s3_features.py) on the release chip_forecast.py sha256 3d02dd3a1bc57e8c53f701a6005c8d5e9d8ad6a15a57cdec3f22b27066015897 and nfa_tasks.npz sha256 e1f056ef33f568052fb8dfdba6e095f7b575c7f78d96768e34469918559008d2.
shared_feeding.row: One (chemical, design, unmeasured tested concentration, output) cell with valid truth.
shared_feeding.ab22: The 22 AnchorBoost features; target = response minus the interpolation anchor.
shared_feeding.raw_long: Long table of the task file: log10 query concentration, the k revealed log10 concentrations, the k revealed readings of the same output, DIV index, feature index (categorical); target = response.
shared_feeding.context: Pooled 10,000 cells sampled without replacement from the full design enumeration of the training chemicals with numpy default_rng(1000 * k + fold) (S1 rule, so the no-structure ab22 table equals S1's E1 context row for row).
shared_feeding.structure: Per-chemical vector -> PCA (16 components) fitted on the fold's training chemicals that have a structure, applied to every chemical; chemicals without a usable structure get NaN. Embeddings: Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits (RDKit); CheMeleon (MIT, Burns et al. 2025, chemprop foundation model, 2048-d); Monroe (MIT, Banaszewski & Fitzgibbon, arXiv 2608.18982, 720-d); KANO (S2's embeddings_kano.npz, 300-d). MotiL embeddings are not on disk (S2 kept only predictions) and are not added. Structures: sota_baselines_2/structures/structures.json (237 of 243 resolved).

LimiX-2.source: github.com/limix-ldm-ai/LimiX commit 516bf396333feb3198cf7aff8a6c10421f218e24 (StableAI License v1.0, Apache-2.0-derived code); weights huggingface.co/stable-ai/LimiX-2 revision de07b679e74a41b50b9de18251a8fa245e537440, LimiX-2.ckpt (StableAI LimiX Non-Commercial License); arXiv 2609.17488.
LimiX-2.settings: LimiXPredictor(device cuda, inference_config config/reg_default_noretrieval_v2.json, mix_precision True, seed 0, categorical_features_indices = DIV and feature index), Kaggle T4. No flash-attn on T4 (SDPA path).

candidates.LX-A: ab22, pooled 10k context, library mean output
candidates.LX-B: ab22, pooled 10k, median of the member-averaged bucket distribution (same logits, decoded at the 0.5 quantile; the library's affine de-standardisation is kept)
candidates.LX-E: ab22, pooled 30,000-row context (same seed rule), mean; 45-minute cap on one T4, recorded as not completed if it overruns

TabImpute.source: pip tabimpute 0.0.4 (source jacobf18/tabular), weights huggingface.co/Tabimpute/TabImpute revision 96d7a0f160184cfb361a03559430baf1cf31aec5 (apache-2.0): tabimpute_001.ckpt (v1, entry-wise features, ImputePFN) and tabimputev2.ckpt (v2, cell-grid axial attention, TabImputeV2); arXiv 2510.02625.
TabImpute.layout_note: The task file's literal layout (one row per chemical, 35 x 68 = 2,380 columns, test row holding only the k revealed cells) gives v1 an entry-wise feature matrix of about 464,000 rows x 2,577 features per design, beyond any GPU; v1 is therefore run on per-output tables and v2, which reads the cell grid directly, runs the literal layout as TI-D.
TabImpute.settings: Matrix per test design: rows = chemicals, test row holds only its k revealed cells, training rows hold all their measured cells, NaN elsewhere; package normalisation and median decoding; float32 on T4 (T4 has no bfloat16 tensor cores).

candidates.TI-A: v1, one table per output: test row + 49 training rows drawn at random (4 draws, seed from task_id and output), columns = the test chemical's tested concentrations in ascending order; prediction = mean of the 4 imputations
candidates.TI-B: v2, one table per output: test row + all training chemicals, columns = the test chemical's tested concentrations
candidates.TI-C: v2, one table per design: test row + all training chemicals, columns = tested concentrations x 68 outputs
candidates.TI-D: v2, literal layout: test row + all training chemicals, columns = 35 concentrations x 68 outputs; 60-minute cap for fold 0 on one T4, recorded as not completed if it overruns

TabPFN-3.5 long table + structure.source: tabpfn 9.1.0, ModelVersion.V3_5, tabpfn-v3.5-20260909.safetensors sha256 ece4d67eadfea42eb0e610df5189bea60cb7f31073d81e9c7a019b76eacf0be3 (TABPFN-3.5 Non-Commercial License v1.0, accepted by the host 2026-10-06 04:17 JST); S1's Kaggle environment and weights dataset <redacted-local-metadata>/sota-tabpfn35-weights.
TabPFN-3.5 long table + structure.settings: TabPFNRegressor.create_default_for_version(V3_5, n_estimators=8, random_state=0, fit_mode='fit_with_cache'), DIV and feature index categorical, as S1's frozen E1.
TabPFN-3.5 long table + structure.control: P0 = ab22 without structure = S1's frozen E1; it must reproduce S1's fold-0 1.078 before any structure candidate is read.

candidates.P5: raw_long + CheMeleon PCA-16 (the task file's long table)

selection: Per opponent, the lowest fold-0 k = 3 MAE among its candidates (development_fold0 cohort, 49 chemicals); a candidate within 0.002 of the lowest wins if it is cheaper (fewer context rows, then fewer columns). Every candidate run is recorded; none is dropped. The choice is written to amendments with a UTC time before the opponent's first fold 1-4 run.
readouts: Folds 1-4: k = 3 first for every opponent, then k = 1, 2, 4 for LimiX-2 and TabPFN-3.5 + structure, and for TabImpute when its frozen layout costs under one GPU hour per k. Predictions in kit format (predictions/<opponent>_k{k}.npz), scored with kit score.py.

writer_S3.LimiX-2: k = 3, 194 cohort: 1.165 to 1.195 with the ab22 feeding (TabPFN-2/3.5 and TabICLv2 with the same feeding landed at 1.182-1.189); beating AnchorBoost 1.161 is possible but below even odds; raw_long on fold 0 about 0.04-0.07 worse than ab22.
writer_S3.TabImpute: 1.40 to 1.65; it has no notion that columns are ordered concentrations, so it should sit near SoftImpute (1.462) and behind interpolation (1.345).
writer_S3.TabPFN-3.5 long table + structure: ab22 + structure 1.175 to 1.190 (structure added at most 0.7% to AnchorBoost in S2); raw_long + structure on fold 0 about 0.04-0.07 worse than ab22 + structure; no structure variant beats AnchorBoost.

amendments.finding: TabImpute v1 on CUDA is batch dependent: on one design (68 per-output matrices) the package impute() equals s3_run.impute_batch with one matrix per forward exactly (max difference 0.0), while 17 matrices per forward (the setting of every TI run so far) differ by mean 0.033, max 1.47 per imputed cell in bfloat16 and mean 0.026 in float32 (typical |prediction| 1.26). Three fold 1-4 designs re-imputed with the package API differ from the frozen TI-A predictions by mean 0.017 to 0.041 per cell.
amendments.change: The TabImpute readout becomes the frozen TI-A on folds 1-4 at k = 3 with one matrix per forward (--ti-batch 1, equal to the package API); the 17-per-forward run is kept as a sensitivity row. The fold-0 selection is not redone: TI-A leads TI-B by 0.016 and TI-C/TI-D by 0.17 or more.

Every Monroe-based result (P8, P3, LX-F/LX-Fm, AnchorBoost + Monroe) is reported with the label "leakage risk". Clean counterparts: TabPFN-3.5 P7 (ab22 + CheMeleon PCA-16, median; fold 0 1.0512, second-lowest TabPFN candidate) on folds 1-4 at k = 1-4 (Kaggle); LimiX-2 LX-Dm (ab22 + CheMeleon PCA-16, median, decoded from the LX-D pass) on folds 1-4 at k = 3 once the 4-GPU box is free. Both are fixed configurations named by the controller, not fold-0 selections. The running LX-F folds 1-4 job finishes as planned.
LimiX-2 clean LX-Dm on folds 1-4 at k = 1, 2, 3, 4 (k = 3 on box 54445594 after the LX-F job; k = 1, 2, 4 on two more 4 x A100 boxes, folds split by GPU, k = 4 sharded in two halves).
